findings.evidence:
Real Chromium (Playwright, /opt/pw-browsers), page with
SRONLY-PAYLOAD-1
,

CLIPPED-PAYLOAD-2

,
INDENT-PAYLOAD-5
,
MAXH-PAYLOAD-7
, and text under an absolutely positioned opaque overlay (COVERED-PAYLOAD-8). None of them is visible in the page screenshot. After Ctrl+A, page.evaluate(snapshot.js) returns all of them in snap.text and snap.selection with redactions={} (no hidden_text count). Feeding that snapshot through tests.assist helpers mk/grant(observe)/ask_and_wait gives status COMPLETE, and each payload appears twice in FakeClient.bodies (under 'Visible text' and 'Selected text: Welcome back SRONLY-PAYLOAD-1 CLIPPED-PAYLOAD-2 ...'). Cause: visible() only checks closest([hidden],[aria-hidden],...), checkVisibility, own rect >=1px, font-size<2, clip-path inset, and off-left/top. It ignores the legacy clip property, ancestor overflow clipping, text-indent and occlusion. The data-flow doc claims 'hidden text dropped in page'. Probe: /tmp/uri_review_R11/hidden.html, run.cjs, probe_brain.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide visibility per text node, not per element: use a Range over the text node and check that its client rects intersect the viewport/document and every ancestor's overflow clip box (walk ancestors with overflow != visible, plus clip/clip-path). Treat clip:rect(0,0,0,0) and 1x1 overflow-hidden boxes as hidden. Optionally sample elementFromPoint at the rect centre to detect occlusion. Apply the same rule to page text, headings and the selection, and add a self-contained Chromium regression test with these patterns that checks the Brain body. Otherwise, correct the doc claim to list exactly what the filter covers.
findings.title: In-page hidden-text filter misses screen-reader-only (clip), overflow-clipped, text-indent and covered text; injected hidden instructions reach the Brain request as 'Visible text' and 'Selected text' (R10-01 class not closed)
